🚨🇲🇽 SHEINBAUM: US MEDDLING SPLIT THE SINALOA CARTEL AND UNLEASHED THE VIOLENCE

The bloodshed tearing through Sinaloa started with a US operation, Sheinbaum said: Washington's deal with one faction to grab Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada fractured the cartel and "generó mucha violencia." Her answer isn't more US agents on Mexican soil — it's Mexican institutions doing the job, with homicides now down to 50.4 a day under a coordinated, sovereign security strategy.

🇲🇽💰 MEXICO WON'T TAX YOUR INHERITANCE — AND WON'T RAISE A SINGLE TAX

Sheinbaum flatly rejected a proposal to tax inheritances — "No estoy de acuerdo con eso" — and refused to open the debate. No inheritance tax, no new taxes, no fiscal reform, while spending on health and education climbs over 20% this year. The 4T funds the poor by ending neoliberal-era corruption, not by squeezing working families.

🇲🇽✊ The owner of Merlín — the World Cup's viral duck — was living with her kids in a storefront. Now she's getting a home. "It's not a gift; through INVI she buys the house little by little." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, July 10 Karla Ivette Gómez lived on Vertiz and Arcos de Belén. Housing as a right, with dignity — not charity.

🇲🇽🎨 Mexico's artisans will be paid royalties — not just for their labor. "The payment model includes compensation for the labor plus royalties on the sale price." — Marina Núñez, Ministry of Culture, Mañanera, July 10 41 master artisans, 21 pieces, sold through Fonart. Authorship recognized — the opposite of the brands that have long copied Indigenous designs and paid nothing.

🇲🇽🇻🇪 250 Mexican rescuers are still in Venezuela. They've pulled two people from the rubble alive. "Seven emergency power plants went by air; Navy ships carry the provisions. Our rescue teams stay deployed." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, July 10 Two quakes (7.2 and 7.5) killed 1,719 people. Mexico answered with brigades, power, and food — solidarity between peoples.

🇲🇽🎨 A turquoise-mosaic Mixtec skull just came home — from the Netherlands. "It is not just objects: it is the memory and identity of the peoples of Mexico returning to where they belong." — Joel Omar Vázquez Herrera, INAH Director, Mañanera, July 10 It now sits in Villa de Tututepec, Oaxaca. A carved Maya panel from Yaxchilán also returned — this one from New York.

🇲🇽🎨 Mexico has recovered 3,716 looted archaeological pieces in 21 months — 10x Peña Nieto's entire term. "We are working to recover and repatriate the memory and identity of the peoples of Mexico." — Joel Omar Vázquez Herrera, INAH Director, Mañanera, July 10 The US returned the most: 3,369 pieces. Across the whole Fourth Transformation, 17,878 objects have come home.

🇲🇽🌎 "Collaboration without subordination." Sheinbaum drew the line between her security policy and the past. — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, July 10 Under Calderón, US agents were allowed to operate on Mexican soil. Her homicide data showed those years — of subordination — ended in more killings, not fewer.
